images.title: Angles from one arm
images.purpose: Angles that share an arm can be read from the same 0 line: ∠POQ is 35° and ∠POR is 95°, so ∠QOR is 60°.
images.composition: Three rays fanning from one point, white space all round.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal base ray OP in grey #6B7280. From the centre O two more rays: OQ at exactly 35 degrees and OR at exactly 95 degrees from OP. The angle POQ is shaded teal #0072B2 and the angle QOR is shaded amber #E69F00. All rays equal length, small arcs. Exactly 3 rays, 2 shaded angles.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the following: more rays than stated
images.takeaway: The angle between two rays is the difference of their readings.
images.description: A base ray OP and two rays OQ and OR at 35 and 95 degrees, with the angle POQ teal marked 35 and the angle QOR amber marked 60.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the teal angle and the amber angle and say how 35 and 60 make 95.

image_decisions.why: Reading several angles from one base arm is one picture of three rays from a point.
